events.continuity_hook: Completes the Minneapolis conference plan after the setup and teardown timing questions are resolved.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the conference flights, hotel, return timing, seat request, and concise calendar summary.
events.scenario_brief: The booth manager confirms teardown should run too late for a comfortable Wednesday-night departure, so Jonah settles on a Thursday return instead of rushing out after the show. The selected plan is a Sunday Bay Area departure that reaches Minneapolis with ample margin before booth setup, the better-rated North Loop hotel with walkable dinner options and practical convention-center access, and a Thursday late-morning return. The remaining notes are to keep the hotel rate cancellable until the booth schedule is fully locked and to request a window seat if seat selection is open.

events.continuity_hook: Adds a practical package-handling check to the already booked Minneapolis conference itinerary.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm hotel package handling, late-arrival handling, and seat details without reopening the full trip search.
events.scenario_brief: Marketing now wants to send a small literature box and badge-scanner kit to Jonah’s hotel before the Minneapolis conference instead of carrying everything through the airport. Jonah needs to verify whether the North Loop hotel will accept and hold the packages until his Sunday arrival, whether any handling fee applies, and whether a late check-in note is needed if the outbound flight slips. The flight plan stays unchanged, but he also wants a quick check that the outbound seat assignment is still in place.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new distributor-training trip after the Minneapolis conference logistics are mostly settled.
events.interaction_goal: Build a flight-and-hotel shortlist that protects the Thursday setup time and leaves the equipment-shipping decision visible.
events.scenario_brief: A distributor in Spokane asks Jonah to lead a Thursday product training and a Friday morning partner check at a Spokane Valley warehouse. He needs Bay Area flight options into Spokane that arrive Wednesday with enough time for setup and avoid a drawn-out connection, plus hotel options near Spokane Valley or downtown with strong guest feedback, parking, reliable early-morning access to the warehouse, and easy dinner choices. The open item is whether the demo case should ship to the distributor or to the hotel.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Spokane planning after the training start time becomes stricter and the hotel trade-off narrows.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the safer outbound timing, compare the hotel-location trade-off, and decide how to handle the demo case shipment.
events.scenario_brief: The distributor moves the Thursday training start earlier because two municipal operators can only attend first thing in the morning. Jonah now rules out Thursday same-day travel and compares a Wednesday afternoon itinerary with one clean connection against a later nonstop that would make hotel arrival tight. The hotel choice has narrowed to a Spokane Valley property closer to the warehouse but with thinner dining nearby versus a better-reviewed downtown option with a longer morning drive.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Spokane distributor-training trip from comparison to booking after the equipment-shipping question is settled.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize flights, hotel, room notes, seat request, and a clean itinerary summary for the training trip.
events.scenario_brief: The distributor confirms the demo case can go directly to the warehouse, so Jonah no longer needs hotel package acceptance for Spokane. The selected plan is a Wednesday afternoon Bay Area departure with one manageable connection, a Friday afternoon return after the partner check, and the better-rated Spokane Valley hotel because it keeps the morning drive short while still offering nearby dinner options. He wants the room notes to request a coffee maker and mini-fridge, and a window seat if available.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new client-site visit after the Spokane distributor trip is booked and Jonah’s next utility visit comes into view.
events.interaction_goal: Create a flight-and-hotel shortlist that protects the early site-access window and keeps the possible extra night flexible.
events.scenario_brief: A water authority in the Hampton Roads area asks Jonah to attend a membrane-system assessment with a Tuesday noon pre-walk and a Wednesday 6:30 a.m. plant-access window. He needs to compare Bay Area routes into Norfolk against using Richmond with a longer drive, with priority on a reliable Monday arrival and no awkward multi-stop itinerary. Hotel options need to be convenient for the early plant drive, have solid guest feedback, parking, and practical evening dining; the unresolved question is whether the client will require him to stay through Thursday for a second operator session.
